title: Project registry (projects.yml)
description: Checked in pre-commit and CI. Rules that span several projects (unique names, subdomains and deploy keys) or several fields (health inside paths, a name in both env and secrets) are checked by the playbook (roles/projects/tasks/validate.yml); Terraform checks subdomains too.

name.description: Directories, registry entry and, with a database, the database and user (with - turned into _).

subdomain.description: DNS record (Terraform) and Caddy site. "@" is the root domain, and also gets www redirected to it. Without one, the project is internal: no DNS record, no Caddy site, and only a backend.

title.description: Shown on the placeholder page. Defaults to name.

repo.description: Linked from the placeholder page. Optional: leave it out for private repositories.

database.description: A PostgreSQL database and user for the backend. The playbook never drops it: while it exists on the server, removing the project or setting false fails the playbook until it is retired by hand (ansible/README.md).

permissions_policy.description: The Permissions-Policy header of the site and its backend, replacing roles/caddy's default (caddy_permissions_policy, which turns off the camera, microphone, location and other powerful features). Write the whole policy, such as "camera=(self), microphone=(), geolocation=()": each feature off (()), for the site itself ((self)), or for any origin (*). Only with a subdomain.

deploy_key.description: Public ed25519 key of the project's CI. Its authorized_keys line is fixed to deploying this project only: its site, its backend or both. Without it, the project cannot be deployed.

allOf.description: Without a subdomain, nothing is public: no site, and a backend Caddy does not reach, so it has no port, health path, paths or private paths (the image's own HEALTHCHECK says whether it is healthy).
With a subdomain, Caddy reaches the backend on its port and checks its health path.
At least one component: a site or a backend.
Only a backend can use a database. Its roles are named after the project plus _app, which PostgreSQL limits to 63 characters.
Migrations and a database URL scheme need a database.
With a site, the backend only gets the paths listed.
Without a site, the backend gets every path.

image.description: Image repository without a tag or digest, such as ghcr.io/abrunacci/epb-stock-backend. CI sends the digest of each deploy, and the server records it.

port.description: Port it listens on, for Caddy. Only with a subdomain.

health.description: Health check path, with the prefix: Caddy does not strip it. Checked from Caddy's container after each deploy; any 2xx answer is healthy. Only with a subdomain.

paths.description: Caddy path matchers sent to the backend, such as /api/*.

private_paths.description: Caddy path matchers of the backend that the internet must never reach, such as /api/ingest: Caddy answers them 404, even inside paths. Only containers that share a network with the backend may call them. Only with a subdomain.

env.description: Non-secret environment variables, public like the rest of this file. Values are strings: quote numbers and booleans.

secrets.description: Secret environment variables: only their names are here, the values live on the server. generated: created once on the server (64 hex characters). manual: set by the admin with project-secret. {from: PROJECT, key: KEY}: the value of another project's secret, copied by the server, which also gives this backend a private network to that project's backend (link-PROJECT).

migrate.description: Command that applies the migrations, run in a one-off container of the new image before each deploy switches to it, such as [alembic, upgrade, head]. It gets MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL and APP_DB_USER.

database_url_scheme.description: Scheme of DATABASE_URL and MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL, such as postgresql+psycopg for SQLAlchemy with psycopg 3. Defaults to postgresql.

memory.description: Memory limit of the container, from 64m to 512m. Defaults to 256m.

max_body.description: Largest request body Caddy passes to the backend, in KB or MB, such as 64KB for a form. Larger ones get 413 without reaching it. Defaults to 10MB. Only with a subdomain.

cpus.description: CPU limit of the container, in CPUs, from 0.1 to 1 (the Droplet has one). Defaults to 0.5.

log_alerts.description: Log lines of the backend to be emailed about (log-alerts, every 5 minutes, one email per run). The lines are emailed as they were logged: only match lines without personal data. Rule names are unique within the backend: checked by the playbook.

log_alert.description: A line matches when every pattern in match is found in it.

name.description: Shown in the email's subject, such as jump_confirmed.

match.description: Python regular expressions, each searched anywhere in the line. Single-quote them in YAML, so backslashes stay as written.

note.description: What the line means and whether anything must be done: the email's first line.

subject.description: How to build the email's subject from the line: a Python regular expression with named groups, and a format that uses them as {group}. A line it does not fit gets the generic subject, PROJECT: NAME, and is emailed all the same.

secret_link.description: Another project's secret, by project name and key. That project must have a backend with a port, and declare the key as generated or manual: checked by the playbook.

env_name.description: An environment variable name. The ones the infrastructure sets itself (per-project databases) are reserved.
